basis: Intestinal motility failure defines the disease; its varied causes do not establish other organ involvement.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; cortical abnormalities 9/9 and retinal dysplasia 6/6.
Pathological vascular ingrowth into the cornea; infectious and immune causes are alternatives, not defining mechanisms.
Primary neoplasm of the splenic red-pulp sinuses; immunological associations do not establish immune-mediated disease.
Intellectual developmental disorder; sensorineural hearing impairment affects 12/21 (~57%). Hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with cerebral atrophy; optic atrophy is occasional (5-29%); feeding difficulty alone adds no organ.
Defining skeletal dysplasia and dentinogenesis imperfecta; pulmonary hypoplasia in 4/10 (40%). Renal disease reported in 1/10.
Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Umbrella for antibody immunodeficiency syndromes; subtype-specific skin, lung and other complications cannot be generalized.
Carcinoma of the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
Meningeal-origin tumour defined by its intraorbital location, commonly involving the optic nerve sheath.
Skin fibrosis and fixed joint contractures define disease; myopia in 6/8 (75%) supports ocular dysfunction. Reflux is separately diagnosed; neuropathy 2/8 is below threshold.
Progressive retinal and choroidal atrophy causes visual loss; optic-disc proximity does not establish extraocular neurologic disease.
Localized sclerosing bone disorder of the medial clavicle; neither infection nor an immune-mediated mechanism is established.
Polydactyly defines syndrome; neurodevelopmental abnormalities 2/2, ocular malformations 1/2, ASD 1/1. Renal agenesis 1/3 omitted by cap; very small cohort.
Malignancy originates in the abdominal peritoneum; ascites reflects local disease. Coagulation abnormalities and ileus are occasional.
Immune-mediated inflammation damages the limbic brain; the associated cancer is a separate disease.
Isolated vaginal developmental malformation; reproductive anatomy falls outside the axes.
Retinal dystrophy and CNS hypomyelination with abnormal very-long-chain fatty acid metabolism; cleft palate reported in 1/1, with substantial frequency uncertainty.
Skeletal myopathy caused by an inborn mitochondrial metabolic defect; additional organs vary across the many subtypes.
Hereditary variation in severity of group A streptococcal infection; no specific damaged anatomical organ is established.
Neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; ptosis and ophthalmoplegia reported in 1/1. Respiratory weakness does not establish direct lung disease.
Sparse record identifies a hairline-related syndrome; dermatologic assignment is provisional, with no evidence establishing other organ involvement.
Defined as disease of blood and blood-forming organs; no additional axis applies across this broad umbrella.
Mitochondrial disorder with defining optic atrophy; neurologic dysfunction is common (~30% or more) across subtypes. Hearing involvement varies; umbrella frequency uncertain.
